correctness.rationale: The resonance straddles the single minimum, so 0 < nx_n < y_B. Comparing f_B(y/(n+1)) with f_B(y/n) at y=nx_n brackets the next short-wave wavenumber strictly between nx_n and y_B; taking the increasing limit gives y_B. For the Taylor inversion, f_B(t)-1=t tanh(t)(B-g(t)) with g(t)=(t coth(t)-1)/t². The sign of t³ sinh²(t)g'(t) is that of cosh(2t)-1-(t/2)sinh(2t)-t², whose series starts in degree six and has strictly negative coefficients thereafter. Thus f'_B(y_B)>0 and Taylor inversion first for nx_n and then division by n gives the stated n^-3 correction and O_B(n^-5). At criticality y_B→0 and y_B²=45δ(1+O(δ)) from its root equation. Dividing the difference of the two even Taylor series by (nx_n)²-x_n² leaves an O((nx_n)^4)=O(δ²) remainder with an n-independent bound, giving the uniform critical claim. For the weak-tension limit write α=nB and use the sign of the exact matching residual at test x: the limits of F/(n-1) at x=c/√α for α→0, F/n at x=c for α→α₀∈(0,∞), and BF at x=c/α for α→∞ are respectively 1-c², tanh(c)-α₀c² and c-c². Each gives two-sided bracketing, and the monotone profile tanh(x)/x² has the required two edges. Compactifying α covers every possible sequence that could violate the supremum claim. This is an analytic audit; verify.py was inspected, not run, and its reported 329 floating-point tests are not used as evidence of uniform convergence. Only linear phase-speed matching is certified by this reasoning.

value.rationale: The short-wave limit and approach identify a physical wavelength that persists as the fundamental wavelength diverges. More importantly, uniformity across harmonic orders resolves how the dispersion matching switches between two different weak-tension scalings and makes the critical coefficient useful without fixing n first. This is a meaningful distinction for selecting resonant linear wave modes, not a claim about nonlinear existence or stability.
